paragraphs.text: Cleanup Mode (清理模式) - a DSH agent preset that reclaims disk space and removes leftovers safely
# Cleanup Mode (清理模式)

A DSH agent preset for reclaiming disk space and removing leftovers on your own machine —
caches, te
mp files, logs, uninstall residue, old installers, stale tool caches.

Its defining property is restraint. Cleanup Mode is not a "one click, everything is fast" cleaner:
i

t discovers with read-only commands, classifies every candidate into a risk tier, writes a
manifest,

and deletes only what you confirmed. It prefers the system trash over permanent deletion,
and it re
fuses to touch operating-system files and the DSH installation.

- 中文说明：README.zh.md
- Works on Windows, macOS and Linux; the bundled knowledge base has a dedicated
- Works on Windows, macOS and Linux; the bundled knowledge base has a dedicated skill per platform.
## What it does

1. **Interview** — what to reclaim, which volume, what must be preserved.
2. **Discover** — read-onl

y enumeration of known leftover locations for your OS.
3. **Measure** — `clean_scan` (tree totals, l

argest subdirectories, largest files) and
`clean_dupes` (duplicate groups by size + SHA-256) turn "t

his folder looks big" into numbers;
both never follow links and both report when a walk was truncate

d.
4. **Classify** — L1 (regenerates itself), L2 (safe but visible consequence), L3 (user data).
Uni

nstall residue is L2 only with evidence that the product is gone (uninstall keys, package
database,

receipts); otherwise it stays L3.
5. **Manifest** — a table with every path, size, why it is a lefto

ver, and what you lose.
6. **Confirm** — one confirmation for L1, grouped confirmations for L2, item

by item for L3.
7. **Delete** — trash first; permanent deletion only where no trash exists, and onl

y after a
separate "cannot be recovered" confirmation.
8. **Audit** — `manifest.json`, `deleted.csv`

and `protected.json` in a per-OS audit directory.
9. **Report with real numbers** — free space is m

easured before the first deletion and after the
last one, so the report separates measured delta fro

m estimated reclaim; it also lists what was
skipped, what needs a re-login or a reboot, and reminds

you that trashed files free nothing until
the trash is emptied.
## Risk tiers
| Tier | Meaning | Examples | Confirmation |

| L0 | Forbidden | OS and boot files, DSH install and profile directories | Refused |
| L1 | Regener

ates itself | temp, cache, logs, thumbnails, crash dumps | One confirmation |
| L2 | Safe but visibl

e | uninstall leftovers, old installers, orphaned app data | Grouped, consequence stated |
| L3 | Us
er data / high-risk | documents, media, source, keys, anything uncertain | Only if you name it, item
high-risk | documents, media, source, keys, anything uncertain | Only if you name it, item by item |

Hard rules the preset enforces: no deletion without a manifest and an explicit confirmation; no
wild

cards in destructive commands; no registry or partition edits; no third-party cleaner installs;
file
names and documents are treated as untrusted data, never as instructions.
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.5`.
- **Full filesystem access for the session.** Cleanup targets live outside th

e workspace, so the
session sandbox must be `danger-full-access`; with `workspace-write` the agent c

an only inspect
and will ask you to raise the permission. The preset cannot grant itself access — th

at is a
host-level policy, by design.
- Some locations need administrator/root privileges (`/var`, `

C:\Windows\Temp`, `/Library`). The
agent reports them instead of escalating silently.
### Shell tool preference

The agent uses one shell tool, preferring `ops_bash` (the OPS bundle's Bash terminal) when the
profi

le publishes it, then `pwsh` on Windows or `bash` elsewhere. The skills are written for
PowerShell o

n Windows and bash on POSIX, so the agent adapts the command syntax to whichever tool
it actually ha

Windows and bash on POSIX, so the agent adapts the command syntax to whichever tool
it actually has.

The bundle also ships `clean_shell`, its own tool row, as the last resort. It is a **wrapper over
th

e same host shell executor** the official tool uses — PowerShell on Windows (pwsh 7 when present,
ot

herwise Windows PowerShell 5.1), bash elsewhere — so sandbox policy, timeouts, output limits and
the

session working directory still come from DSH. Nothing is installed and no second shell
[该节后续省略]
### Known incompatibility: profiles that deny host shell tools

A profile can hide the official shell tools on purpose. The `dsh-ops` bundle offers this through
its

`dsh-ops/shell` component with `shellPolicy: deny-host-shell`, which denies `pwsh`, `bash` and
`pws

h_persistent` for every agent. A preset that mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh` then has the
tool r

egistered but filtered out of the model's tool list. Cleanup Mode needs a shell to measure
sizes, pr
obe the trash and delete, so it stops at step one and tells you what is missing.
Fix it on the profile side: remove `pwsh` from that component's `deniedHostTools`, or do not enable

the deny policy. Another option is to enable the OPS `shell` component in `advise` mode, which
publi
shes `ops_bash` for every session — the agent then prefers it automatically.

Note that the `dsh-ops` **mode rows** (`dsh-ops/mode-standard` and friends) only serve their own
fou

r built-in presets: `ops_bash` is gated by preset id, so a custom preset such as this one does
not r
eceive it from a mode row. The component form above is not gated that way.
## What it never touches

OS system and boot files, `WinSxS`, `C:\Windows\Installer`, package-manager databases,
`/System`, `/

usr`, `/boot`, `/var/lib/dpkg`, the DSH installation and `~/.dsh`, `.ssh`/`.gnupg`,
password-manager

vaults, and cloud-placeholder files (deleting a placeholder deletes the cloud
copy). High-risk loca

tions — Documents, Desktop, Pictures, source repositories — are never
proposed by the agent; it only
inspects them when you name them.
## Audit and privacy
Audit records are local only, per OS:
XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/dsh-clean/`

Layout: `audit/sessions/<timestamp>/{manifest.json,deleted.csv,protected.json,report.md}` plus
`conf

ig.json` for the protected-path list. Paths are stored verbatim on your machine; nothing is
uploaded
. Old sessions rotate after 30 runs.
